pka_pka-compilation-williams.cite: R. Williams, pKa Data Compiled (ACS Organic Division, updated 4/7/2022), via OrganicChemistryData.org
pka_pka-compilation-williams.says: Aqueous pKa/pKaH tables, e.g. ammonia 9.21, piperidine 11.22, aniline 4.19, imidazole 6.95, formic acid 3.77, acetylacetone 8.95, p-methoxyphenol 10.16, 4-nitrophenol row 7.14 (PDF text extracted with pdftotext; two-column layout is noisy, so PubChem values are the primary numbers used).

wiki_carbenium.cite: Wikipedia, 'Carbenium ion' (last resort; cites hydride ion affinity data)
wiki_carbenium.says: Hydride ion affinities (kcal/mol) 231, 246, 273, 312 for tBu+, iPr+, Et+, CH3+; stability 3>2>1>methyl.

wiki_bde.cite: Wikipedia, 'Bond-dissociation energy' (last resort; table of C-H BDEs)
wiki_bde.says: C-H BDE (kcal/mol): methyl 105, ethyl 101, isopropyl 99, t-butyl 96.5, alpha-amine 91, alpha-ether 92, alpha-ketone 96, vinyl 111, allylic 89, benzylic 90.

lt_alkstab.cite: OpenStax Organic Chemistry (McMurry) section 7.6 Stability of Alkenes, via LibreTexts
lt_alkstab.says: Heats of hydrogenation (kJ/mol): ethylene -136, propene -125, cis-2-butene -119, trans-2-butene -115, 2-methylpropene -118, 2-methyl-2-butene -112, 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene -110; more substituted = more stable.

os_sn2.cite: OpenStax Organic Chemistry (McMurry) section 11.3 Characteristics of the SN2 Reaction, via LibreTexts
os_sn2.says: Substrate order methyl > primary > isopropyl >> tert-butyl; table of nucleophile relative rates toward CH3Br: H2O 1, acetate 500, NH3 700, Cl- 1000, HO- 10000, MeO- 25000, I- 100000, CN- 125000, HS- 125000.

os_sn1.cite: OpenStax Organic Chemistry (McMurry) section 11.5 Characteristics of the SN1 Reaction, via LibreTexts
os_sn1.says: SN1 reactivity follows carbocation stability 3>2>1>methyl; allylic/benzylic extra stabilized (primary allylic ~ secondary alkyl, secondary allylic ~ tertiary); 3-bromo-1-butene and 1-bromo-2-butene react at nearly the same rate.

wiki_lg.says: In one study (citation needed on the page) reactivity Cl 1 < I 91 < OTs 3.7e4 < OTf 1.4e8; a table of k(X)/k(Br) in two SN2 reactions gives Cl 0.0074/0.0024, I 3.5/1.9, OTs 0.44/3.6, i.e. tosylate placement depends on the nucleophile.

lt_carbonylrx.cite: LibreTexts, Organic Chemistry (Morsch et al.) 21.2 Nucleophilic acyl substitution reactions
lt_carbonylrx.says: Acid halides and anhydrides are most reactive derivatives, amides least; reactivity follows leaving-group ability (conjugate-acid pKa) and carbonyl stabilization by the Y group (the ranking scheme itself is an image, not captured in text).

wiki_carbonyl.says: Qualitative electrophilicity order RCHO > R2CO > RCO2R' > RCONH2.

wiki_hydrate.says: Hydration equilibrium constants: acetone ~1e-3, formaldehyde ~1e3, hexafluoroacetone ~1e6.

pmc_nitration.cite: ACS Omega 2022, 7, 8199 (PMC8928515) Table 3: relative nitration rate constants, via PMC
pmc_nitration.says: log k_rel for nitration (benzene = 0): tBu-benzene 1.29, o-xylene 2.28, mesitylene 2.98, 1,2,3,4-tetramethylbenzene 3.33, fluorobenzene -0.92, iodobenzene -1.00, chlorobenzene -1.52, bromobenzene -1.52.

cases.title: Carboxylic acids: halogenation lowers pKa
cases.uncertainty: Aqueous 25 C values; values for TFA vary 0.2-0.5 between compilations but order is unaffected.
cases.basis: aqueous pKa values (PubChem experimental: TFA 0.3, ClCH2CO2H 2.87, HCO2H 3.742, AcOH 4.756; Williams table formic 3.77)
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Lowest pKa = most acidic = ranked first.

cases.title: Thiols versus alcohols versus phenol: S-H is the more acidic despite lower electronegativity
cases.uncertainty: Phenol (9.99) and ethanethiol (10.61) differ by only 0.6 pKa units; both literature values are aqueous 25 C. Order of S-H vs O-H acids is solvent-dependent in non-aqueous media.
cases.basis: aqueous pKa: benzenethiol 6.62, phenol 9.99, ethanethiol 10.61, 2-propanol 17.1 (PubChem experimental)
cases.tie_tolerance_note: No ties; phenol/ethanethiol are the closest pair.

cases.title: Para-substituted phenols with a near-tied electron-donor pair
cases.uncertainty: 4-methoxyphenol (10.05-10.16) and 4-methylphenol (10.26) differ by 0.1-0.2 pKa units, within inter-laboratory scatter; they are therefore grouped as a tie.
cases.basis: aqueous pKa: 4-nitrophenol 7.15, 4-chlorophenol 9.41, phenol 9.99, 4-methoxyphenol 10.05 (Williams: 10.16), 4-methylphenol 10.26
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Treat |delta pKa| < 0.3 as a tie.

cases.title: C-H acids with two carbonyl/nitro activators versus an alcohol and a ketone
cases.uncertainty: Aqueous scale only. In DMSO the relative acidity of alcohols and simple ketones changes and C-H/O-H ordering is solvent-dependent; acetone pKa is ~19-20 depending on compilation.
cases.basis: aqueous pKa: acetylacetone 8.93, nitromethane 10.21, 2-propanol 17.1, acetone ~20
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Spacing is >1 pKa unit between every adjacent pair.

cases.title: Amines and heteroaromatic amines by conjugate-acid pKa
cases.uncertainty: Aqueous values. Ammonia value derived as 14 - pKb.
cases.basis: pKaH: piperidine 11.12 (Williams 11.22), ammonia ~9.25 (from pKb 4.751; Williams 9.21), pyridine 5.23, aniline 4.6

cases.title: Nitrogen lone pair availability: alkylamine > imidazole > nitroaniline > pyrrole
cases.uncertainty: Pyrrole is protonated at carbon, not nitrogen; its conjugate-acid pKa -3.8 refers to that species.
cases.basis: pKaH: cyclohexylamine 10.63, imidazole 6.95, 4-nitroaniline 1.01, pyrrole -3.80 (protonation on carbon)

cases.title: Primary/secondary/tertiary ethylamines: aqueous order is not monotonic
cases.uncertainty: PubChem lists two values each for ethylamine (10.7, 10.87) and triethylamine (10.78, 10.9) so their order is not resolved; only diethylamine as highest is clear. Solvent-dependent: gas-phase and water orders differ.
cases.basis: aqueous pKaH: diethylamine 11.09, triethylamine 10.78 (also 10.9), ethylamine 10.7 and 10.87
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Triethylamine and ethylamine are within 0.2 pKa units: tie.

cases.title: Conjugate-base stability follows the pKa of the acid
cases.uncertainty: Uses pKa as the experimental proxy for conjugate-base stability (aqueous).
cases.basis: aqueous pKa of the strongest acidic site: acetic acid 4.756, 4-nitrophenol 7.15, phenol 9.99, 2-propanol 17.1

cases.title: Alkyl carbocation stability via hydride ion affinity of the parent hydrocarbons
cases.uncertainty: Molecules are the neutral hydrocarbons; the tertiary C-H of isobutane gives tBu+, propane's secondary site gives iPr+. Gas-phase values, not solution.
cases.basis: gas-phase hydride ion affinities (kcal/mol) of tBu+, iPr+, Et+, CH3+ (lower HIA = more stable cation)

cases.title: Alkyl radical stability from C-H bond dissociation energies
cases.uncertainty: BDE values are +-1-2 kcal/mol; adjacent spacings (2-3.5 kcal/mol) exceed that.
cases.basis: C-H BDE (kcal/mol): t-butyl 96.5, isopropyl 99, ethyl 101, methyl 105 (lower BDE = more stable radical)

cases.title: Allylic and heteroatom-stabilized radicals versus ketone alpha and vinyl
cases.uncertainty: Table rows are model C-H bonds; trimethylamine is matched to the (CH3)2NCH2-H row and THF to the ether row. Propene/trimethylamine/THF differ by only 1-2 kcal/mol, within BDE uncertainty, so their relative order is the weakest part of this case.
cases.basis: C-H BDE (kcal/mol): allylic 89, alpha-to-amine ((CH3)2N-CH2-H) 91, alpha-to-ether 92, alpha-to-ketone 96, vinyl 111
cases.tie_tolerance_note: 89/91/92 kcal/mol are within quoted +-1-2 error; consider tolerance of 2 kcal/mol.

cases.title: Alkene stability by heat of hydrogenation: substitution
cases.basis: heats of hydrogenation (kJ/mol): 2-methyl-2-butene -112, trans-2-butene -115, propene -125, ethylene -136 (less exothermic = more stable)

cases.title: Cis versus trans disubstituted alkenes are not equally stable
cases.uncertainty: cis/trans gap is 4 kJ/mol (equilibrium data give 2.8 kJ/mol); direction is unambiguous.
cases.basis: heats of hydrogenation (kJ/mol): trans-2-butene -115, cis-2-butene -119, propene -125
cases.tie_tolerance_note: A tool that scores only substitution count will tie cis and trans.

cases.title: SN2 substrate steric order with the same leaving group
cases.uncertainty: Source states the order for halides generally and gives no numeric rates for these iodides.
cases.basis: textbook SN2 steric order methyl > primary > secondary >> tertiary (tertiary effectively unreactive)

cases.title: SN1 reactivity follows carbocation stability
cases.uncertainty: No numeric rates in the fetched text; chlorides used (source discusses halides generally).
cases.basis: carbocation stability 3 > 2 > 1 > methyl equals SN1 reactivity order for halides

cases.title: Allylic chlorides: both isomers ionize to the same allylic cation
cases.uncertainty: The source states the tie for the bromides and a stability equivalence in general terms; transferred here to chlorides. Magnitude of the gap to isopropyl chloride is not given.
cases.basis: 3-halo-1-butene and 1-halo-2-butene undergo SN1 at nearly the same rate (same 1-methylallyl cation); a secondary allylic cation is about as stable as a tertiary alkyl one, so both exceed isopropyl and ethyl
cases.tie_tolerance_note: The two allylic chlorides give the same cation and should tie.

cases.title: Methyl electrophiles: chloride, iodide, tosylate, triflate
cases.uncertainty: Source is Wikipedia and the cited study has a 'citation needed' flag; the study's substrate is not stated, so the methyl substrates here are an assumption. The order Cl < I < OTs < OTf itself is textbook-consistent.
cases.basis: relative rates for leaving groups (chloride = 1): iodide 91, tosylate 3.7e4, triflate 1.4e8

cases.title: Condition-dependent: tosylate versus halides
cases.uncertainty: Tosylate is slower than iodide with a soft thiolate nucleophile (0.44 vs 3.5) but faster than iodide with ethoxide (3.6 vs 1.9). The honest answer for tosylate is 'condition dependent'; only I > Cl is solvent- and nucleophile-independent. Source does not state the substrate; ethyl assumed. expected_order lists only the robust part; the tosylate placement should be reported as unranked/condition dependent.
cases.basis: relative rates k(X)/k(Br) in two SN2 reactions: I 3.5/1.9, Cl 0.0074/0.0024, OTs 0.44/3.6
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Tool may place tosylate anywhere; do not score its position.

cases.title: Anionic nucleophiles toward CH3Br
cases.uncertainty: Table is for the textbook's (protic/polar) conditions; in polar aprotic solvents the halide order inverts and OH- exceeds I-.
cases.basis: relative SN2 rates with bromomethane: I- 100000, HO- 10000, Cl- 1000, AcO- 500, H2O 1

cases.title: A neutral nucleophile beats a charged one: ammonia versus acetate
cases.uncertainty: Gaps between 1000/700/500 are small (about 1.4x each) and conditions (solvent) are not specified beyond the table; treat NH3 vs acetate as the least robust pair.
cases.basis: relative SN2 rates with bromomethane: Cl- 1000, NH3 700, acetate 500, H2O 1
cases.tie_tolerance_note: A rule 'anion > neutral' wrongly puts acetate above ammonia.

cases.title: Cyanide and hydrosulfide tie at the top of the table
cases.uncertainty: Table rounds values; I- (1.0e5) is within 25% of CN-/HS- (1.25e5). Solvent-dependent (aprotic solvents change the halide/hydroxide order).
cases.basis: relative SN2 rates with bromomethane: CN- 125000, HS- 125000, I- 100000, HO- 10000
cases.tie_tolerance_note: CN- and HS- are equal in the source; I- within 25% should be treated as a near-tie with them.

cases.title: Acyl-substitution reactivity: acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide
cases.uncertainty: The fetched text states acid halides/anhydrides are most reactive and amides least, and explains the pKa/resonance criteria, but the full ranking scheme is an image not captured as text; acid chloride vs anhydride and anhydride vs ester rest on the standard textbook scheme.
cases.basis: standard ordering of carboxylic acid derivatives by leaving-group ability (conjugate-acid pKa) and carbonyl stabilization

cases.title: Carbonyl electrophilicity: hexafluoroacetone far above acetone, then ester and amide
cases.uncertainty: Hydration K is a thermodynamic proxy for electrophilicity; ester vs amide ranking is qualitative.
cases.basis: hydration equilibrium constants: hexafluoroacetone ~1e6, acetone ~1e-3; ketone > ester > amide electrophilicity (qualitative)

cases.title: Halobenzenes nitration: fluorine is the least deactivating; chloro and bromo tie
cases.uncertainty: F and I differ by only 0.08 log units (a 20% rate difference), so that pair is close; nitration rates may not transfer to other electrophiles.
cases.basis: log k_rel (nitration, benzene = 0): F -0.92, I -1.00, Cl -1.52, Br -1.52
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Cl and Br are equal (-1.52).

cases.title: Alkylbenzenes activate by degree of methylation; fluorobenzene deactivates
cases.basis: log k_rel (nitration, benzene = 0): 1,2,3,4-tetramethylbenzene 3.33, mesitylene 2.98, o-xylene 2.28, tert-butylbenzene 1.29, fluorobenzene -0.92

cases.title: Hammett sigma-para of electron-withdrawing substituents
cases.uncertainty: Cl and Br differ by 0.005 (a tie); sigma_meta order is CF3 0.43 > Br 0.393 > Cl 0.373 > F 0.337, which separates them slightly, so only the tie-tolerant reading is safe.
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Cl/Br tie.

cases.title: Hammett sigma-para of electron-donating substituents (more negative = stronger donor)
cases.uncertainty: N-butylaniline is matched to the 'butylamino' table row.
cases.basis: sigma_para: NMe2 -0.83, NH2 -0.66, NHBu -0.51, OH -0.37

cases.title: Hydrogen bonding versus dipole versus dispersion at similar size
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): 1-butanol 117.7, butanal 74.8, butane -0.5

cases.title: Chain branching lowers boiling point among C5H12 isomers
cases.uncertainty: A size-only (same formula) boiling-point score will tie these three.
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): pentane 36.06, isopentane 27.83, neopentane 9.5
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Score differences are real (8 and 18 C).

cases.title: Lighter hydrogen-bonded alcohol outboils heavier alkane and ether
cases.uncertainty: Molecular weights run 86 (hexane) > 74 (ether) > 60 (propanol) > 58 (acetone), the opposite of the boiling-point order for propanol/ether.
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): 1-propanol 97.2, hexane 68.73, acetone 56.08, diethyl ether 34.6

cases.title: Amide > carboxylic acid > ester > formate ester
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): acetamide 222, acetic acid 117.9, ethyl acetate 77.1, methyl formate 31.5

cases.title: Near-tie: cis- and trans-2-butene
cases.uncertainty: Only 2.9 C between cis and trans (and 1.4 C between trans-2-butene and butane); PubChem's trans-2-butene record lists a first value (3.73) mislabelled as the cis isomer; the trans values used are 0.88/0.9.
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): cis-2-butene 3.73, trans-2-butene 0.88, butane -0.5
cases.tie_tolerance_note: A tolerance of ~3 C would merge cis-2-butene with trans-2-butene.

cases.title: Dichlorobenzene isomers: ortho highest, meta/para nearly tied
cases.uncertainty: para and meta differ by 0.9 C (PubChem also lists a range 173-180.5 for para).
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): o-dichlorobenzene 180.1, p-dichlorobenzene 173.9, m-dichlorobenzene 173
cases.tie_tolerance_note: m/p tie.

cases.title: Enantiomers tie; branching and hydrogen bonding order the butanols
cases.uncertainty: PubChem's bp is for 2-butanol (unspecified/racemic); the identity of enantiomer boiling points is a physical-law inference rather than a quoted value.
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): 1-butanol 117.7, 2-butanol 99.5, tert-butanol 82.3; enantiomers have identical boiling points
cases.tie_tolerance_note: (R)- and (S)-2-butanol must share a group.

cases.title: Alkane chain length, ring and iodoalkane
cases.uncertainty: Iodomethane (MW 142) boils below hexane (MW 86): heavy-atom mass is not the driver.
cases.basis: normal boiling points (C): heptane 98.38, cyclohexane 80.7, hexane 68.73, iodomethane 42.5, pentane 36.06

cases.title: Symmetry: para-dichlorobenzene melts far higher than ortho/meta
cases.uncertainty: ortho and meta differ by only ~8 C.
cases.basis: melting points (C): p 53, o -17, m -24.8
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Boiling-point order for the same set differs (o > p > m), so a single polarity score cannot satisfy both.

cases.title: Neopentane (spherical) melts far above its linear and branched isomers
cases.uncertainty: Branching lowers the boiling point but raises the melting point only for the highly symmetric isomer; isopentane melts below pentane.
cases.basis: melting points (C): neopentane -16.6, pentane -129.67, isopentane -159.8

cases.title: Water solubility of C4-C6 alcohols and alkanes
cases.uncertainty: tert-butanol is miscible; 1000 g/L is a nominal stand-in.
cases.basis: water solubility (g/L, 25 C): tert-butanol miscible (1000 mg/mL), 1-butanol 68, pentane 0.038, hexane 0.0095

cases.title: Two fully miscible liquids tie above ethyl acetate and hexane
cases.uncertainty: 'Miscible' values have no numeric g/L (null). Ethyl acetate listed as 64 g/L and 80 g/L in different records (mid-value 70 shown).
cases.basis: water solubility: acetic acid miscible, diethylamine infinitely soluble, ethyl acetate 64-80 g/L, hexane 9.5 mg/L
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Acetic acid and diethylamine must share the top group.

cases.title: Experimental log Kow across alkane, alcohol, ether, ketone and polyol
cases.uncertainty: Mode says RDKit logP when available; this ordering uses experimental log Kow, and a Crippen logP may deviate for individual molecules.
cases.basis: experimental log Kow: hexane 3.90, 1-pentanol 1.51, diethyl ether 0.89, acetone -0.24, glycerol -1.76

cases.title: Near-tie: diethyl ether and 1-butanol
cases.uncertainty: Ether and butanol differ by 0.01 and the ether value is flagged 'calculated' in one record; ethyl acetate is only 0.15 lower.
cases.basis: experimental log Kow: diethyl ether 0.89 (0.89 calculated per PubChem), 1-butanol 0.88, ethyl acetate 0.73, 1-propanol 0.25, acetic acid -0.17
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Treat |delta logP| < 0.1 as a tie.

cases.title: Hexane, cyclohexane and pentane cluster; iodomethane is lower
cases.uncertainty: Cyclohexane (3.44) and pentane (3.39) differ by 0.05, within measurement scatter (PubChem also lists 3.23 for pentane).
cases.basis: experimental log Kow: hexane 3.90, cyclohexane 3.44, pentane 3.39, iodomethane 1.51
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Cyclohexane/pentane tie.

cases.title: Heavy-atom mass beats carbon count: CH3I outweighs heptane
cases.uncertainty: Molecular ion of the all-12C/1H/16O/127I species; heptane and ether molecular ions are weak in real EI spectra though the m/z is defined.
cases.basis: monoisotopic masses (m/z of M+.): CH3I 141.93, heptane 100.13, cyclohexane 84.09, diethyl ether 74.07

cases.title: Constitutional isomers share the same molecular-ion m/z
cases.basis: monoisotopic masses: hexane 86.11, pentane = isopentane 72.09, butane 58.08
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Pentane and isopentane are identical (C5H12) and must tie.

cases.title: Isomeric C4H8O and acetic acid versus acetone
cases.basis: monoisotopic masses: ethyl acetate 88.05, butanone = THF 72.06, acetic acid 60.02, acetone 58.04
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Butanone and THF are isomers (C4H8O) and must tie; acetic acid vs acetone differ by 2 Da.

cases.title: Number of distinct carbon environments by symmetry
cases.uncertainty: Symmetry-derived counts, not a quoted spectrum; no fetched source lists these specific spectra.
cases.basis: counted from molecular symmetry (proton-decoupled 13C, fast ring flip): methylcyclohexane 5, propane 2, cyclohexane 1, cyclopentane 1
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Cyclohexane and cyclopentane both show one signal.

cases.title: Xylene isomers all have eight carbons but different signal counts
cases.uncertainty: Symmetry-derived counts; no fetched source lists these spectra.
cases.basis: counted from symmetry: m-xylene 5, o-xylene 4, p-xylene 3
cases.tie_tolerance_note: A carbon-count heuristic ties all three.

cases.title: Pentane isomers
cases.uncertainty: Symmetry-derived counts; no fetched source lists these spectra.
cases.basis: counted from symmetry: isopentane 4, pentane 3, neopentane 2

cases.title: Distinct proton environments, ignoring splitting
cases.uncertainty: Symmetry-derived counts; no fetched source lists these spectra. Cyclohexane at low temperature shows axial/equatorial signals; room-temperature fast exchange assumed.
cases.basis: counted from symmetry: isopentane 4 (two equivalent CH3 + CH + CH2 + CH3), pentane 3, neopentane 1, cyclohexane 1 (fast ring flip)
cases.tie_tolerance_note: Neopentane and cyclohexane both show a single signal.

cases.title: Hydrogen-bond donor plus acceptor counts
cases.uncertainty: Structural count (Lipinski-style HBD+HBA), not a measured quantity; no fetched source.
cases.basis: O-H count (donors) plus oxygen lone-pair acceptor sites: glycerol 3+3, 1-butanol 1+1, diethyl ether 0+1, hexane 0
